text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 20 in history:
1597 - William Barents, Dutch explorer who tried to search for the north-east passage, died in the Arctic in the attempt when his ship became trapped in ice.
1624 - France and the United Provinces (Netherlands) signed a treaty of non-aggression at Compiegne.

1756 - Over 140 people who were defending Calcutta were imprisoned by the Nawab of Bengal in the East India Company's jail; 23 survived this imprisonment in what later became known as the Black Hole of Calcutta.
1782 - The Great Seal of the United States government, designed by William Barton, was adopted on this day.

1789 - The newly proclaimed National Assembly in France met on the Jeu de Paume tennis court in Paris. The deputies signed an oath "never to separate and to meet whenever circumstances demand until the Constitution of the Kingdom has been firmly established and consolidated"
1792 - A huge crowd of at least 20,000 stormed the Tuilieries in Paris and tried to negotiate with King Louis XVI.

1819 - Jacques Offenbach, French composer, born as Jakob Eberst. Best known for his light operettas including "Orphee aux enfers" (Orpheus in the Underworld) and one grand opera "Les contes D'Hoffmann" (Tales of Hoffmann).
1819 - The 320-ton paddle-wheel steamship Savannah became the first steamship to cross the Atlantic. It arrived in Liverpool after a journey from Savannah, Georgia, of 27 days 11 hours.
1837 - William IV of Great Britain died at Windsor and was succeeded by his niece Victoria; she reigned until her death in 1901.
1837 - With the accession of Queen Victoria to the British throne, Hanover was automatically separated from Great Britain as its law forbad women to accede to the throne.
1863 - West Virginia was admitted to the Union as the 35th state.
1887 - The longest railway bridge in Britain and the second over the River Tay in Scotland was opened. The first had collapsed in 1879.
1900 - The German ambassador in Peking, Baron von Ketteler, was assassinated by Chinese troops setting off the Boxer Rebellion which sought to remove foreign influence in China.
1909 - Errol Flynn was born in Tasmania. He became one of the great Hollywood screen stars appearing in films including "The Adventures of Robin Hood" "Captain Blood" and " The Sea Hawk".
1923 - Pancho Villa, Mexican revolutionary leader, was assassinated on his farm.
1940 - The French Government requested an armistice with Italy in World War Two.
1944 - The battle of the Philippine Sea ended with Japan losing almost its remaining trained pilots and at least 4,000 seamen.
1963 - Russia and the United States agreed to establish a hot-line telephone link; it was opened on August 30.
1969 - In Rhodesia, a referendum held on the proposed constitution resulted in a landslide victory for Ian Smith's proposals for a republic.
1994 - A bomb tore through Moslem worshippers at the Imam Reza mausoleum in Mashhad, northeast Iran, killing at least 25 people and wounding 70.

1995 - After mounting pressure from the environmental group Greenpeace and government ministers in Germany, Sweden, Denmark and elsewhere, Shell oil company decided not to dump the disused oil rig Brent Spar in the North Atlantic.
